Can you write off a new laptop all at once? This year, yes. From January, no.
Our Manitoba freelancer nets sixty thousand and buys a two-thousand-dollar laptop, used only for work.
A laptop isn't a regular expense. It's equipment: class fifty, claimed at fifty-five percent a year.
But for computers bought and put to use before twenty twenty-seven, the first-year claim is one hundred percent. All two thousand.
That saves this freelancer about seven hundred and eleven dollars in tax and CPP, this year.
Same laptop in January? Year one is fifty-five percent: eleven hundred. Saved: about three ninety.
The other nine hundred trickles in over the next few years.
The honest part: spending two thousand to save seven hundred is still spending. Buy it because you need it.
And when you sell the old laptop, there's a catch.
